assumptions: Assays (capture reagents, particle counting, and omics assays) have been pre-checked for buffer compatibility and include spike-in controls to detect assay failure.
Sufficient material yield exists to perform fraction-level protected-cargo assays on >=3 independent production lots.
biological_rationale: Rodent functional data indicate reproducible bioactivity in conditioned-medium-derived materials, but MISEV2023 and limited large-animal biodistribution raise concern that bulk particle or soluble-protein measures conflate non-EV co-isolates with bona fide EV cargo. A focused protected multi-analyte fingerprint, measured on immuno-captured, particle-peak fractions and shown to be detergent/protease-sensitive, provides an operational test of whether conserved, EV-associated cargo exists across lots without asserting a single mechanistic molecule.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Qualitative presence/absence of each panel member in capture-positive particle-peak fractions and qualitative loss after detergent+protease treatment (membrane protection).
candidate_quality_attributes.name: Protected-cargo composite fingerprint (panel-level, qualitative)
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: A small, predefined panel of protected miRNAs and detergent/protease-sensitive luminal proteins measured on capture-positive, particle-peak fractions enables a practical, lot-level qualitative gate distinguishing EV-associated cargo from secretome co-isolates without presuming a single active molecule.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: Moderate: panel selection is operator-dependent and sensitivity in low-biomass capture fractions is uncertain.

edges.competing_explanation: Apparent protected-cargo conservation could reflect consistent co-isolation of abundant soluble complexes or assay cross-reactivity rather than true EV-protected cargo.
edges.missing_experiment: Cross-lot protected-cargo profiling on immuno-captured particle-peak fractions with detergent/protease controls and spike-in controls to exclude assay bias.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: guidance supports protected-cargo linkage to EV identity; rodent efficacy shows activity but does not define protected cargo; detection in larger species remains uncertain.

nodes.statement: If a membrane-protected, capture-positive particle fraction contains a reproducible composite of protected miRNAs and detergent/protease-sensitive luminal proteins across independent lots, then that composite is an EV-associated cargo fingerprint distinct from variable secretome co-isolates.

If the composite fingerprint is absent or inconsistent across lots or is detergent-insensitive, then observed cargo signals likely reflect non-vesicular secretome co-isolates or assay artifacts and cannot be used to gate lots as EV-enriched.

competing_explanations: Conserved cargo signals may arise from tightly bound soluble complexes or lipoproteins that co-elute with particles and appear detergent-sensitive due to assay interference, not true membrane protection.
Apparent conservation could be driven by upstream source-cell consistency (donor genetics or culture conditions) rather than an EV-specific packaging program.
dependencies: Analytical validation of capture-reagent compatibility with chosen buffers and reagents
Selection and pre-validation of the small protected-cargo panel (operator to nominate candidates based on literature and pilot data)
Sourcing of an orthogonal exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer
design_question: Which focused, protected multi-analyte cargo panel (selected protected miRNAs + protected luminal proteins) reproducibly co-occurs in capture-positive, particle-peak fractions across independent lots and thereby discriminates EV-associated cargo from variable secretome co-isolates without presuming a single active molecule?
expected_measurable_effect: Qualitative, reproducible detection (present/absent) of the predefined protected-cargo panel in capture-positive, particle-peak fractions across >=3 independent lots and loss or marked reduction of those signals after detergent + protease/RNase treatment (indicating membrane protection).

experiment.assay: Orthogonal fraction-level workflow: (1) fractionate sample (density/SEC) and record particle counts per fraction; (2) immuno-capture on intact, particle-peak fractions and eluate capture material; (3) split eluates ± detergent + protease/RNase and perform targeted miRNA panel assays and targeted proteomics on each split; (4) measure total protein and compute protein:particle context for fractions; (5) evaluate spike-in tracer recovery in same fractions.
experiment.comparator: Per-lot matched pair: (A) bounded, capture-positive particle-peak fractions (from enriched small-EV workflow) versus (B) concentrated conditioned-medium (secretome-retaining) fractions processed identically; both spiked with exogenous tracer prior to fractionation. Include detergent+protease-treated aliquots for each fraction.
experiment.control: Positive control: characterized small EV preparation processed in parallel and spike-in tracer recovery; Negative controls: buffer-only fractions and detergent-disrupted samples. Spike-in tracer used to confirm fraction-level assay recovery.
dependencies: Availability of >=3 independent production lots with sufficient yield
Validated capture reagents and particle-count instrumentation
Access to targeted miRNA and targeted proteomics platforms with spike-in normalization capability
Pre-validated buffer-compatibility and spike-in recovery controls
experiment.failure_criterion: If spike-in controls validate assay recovery but endogenous protected-cargo panel members are absent or not detergent/protease-sensitive in capture-positive fractions across >=3 lots, the hypothesis is falsified and the material should be treated as lacking a reproducible EV-associated cargo fingerprint for lot gating.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If falsified, the program must not use the protected-cargo fingerprint as an EV-associated lot gate, and should revert to alternative fractionation, tighter source-cell controls, or secretome-centric product definitions while re-evaluating panel selection and assay sensitivity.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: A focused protected-cargo composite fingerprint (selected protected miRNAs + detergent/protease-sensitive luminal proteins) will be reproducibly detected in capture-positive particle-peak fractions across independent lots and will be substantially reduced or abolished after detergent + protease/RNase treatment, whereas concentrated conditioned-medium controls will lack this protected fingerprint or show detergent-insensitive signals.
experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative presence/absence call for the protected-cargo panel members in capture-positive, particle-peak fractions across >=3 lots, AND qualitative loss (present -> absent or substantially reduced) of those signals after detergent + protease/RNase treatment in the same fractions.
experiment.question: Does a small, predefined protected-cargo panel (3–6 miRNAs + 2–4 luminal proteins) reproducibly occur in immuno-capture-positive, particle-peak fractions across >=3 independent production lots and is that signal membrane-protected (lost after detergent + protease/RNase)?
required_material: >=3 independent conditioned-medium production lots from the same source-cell bank/passage range processed identically
Immuno-capture reagents for intact EV surface markers (anti-CD63, anti-CD9, anti-CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5)
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Density-gradient (iodixanol) or SEC fractionation materials and fraction collectors
Exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer (orthogonal species or isotope-labeled) for assay recovery controls
Protease (proteinase K), RNase reagents and detergent (Triton X-100 or equivalent) for membrane-disruption controls
Reagents for targeted small-RNA measurement (RT-qPCR or targeted sequencing) with spike-in controls
Targeted proteomics reagents (SRM/PRM) for selected luminal proteins and appropriate standards
Total protein assay reagents and consumables
secondary_readouts: Spike-in tracer recovery and membrane-protection behavior per fraction (validates assay recovery)
Protein:particle ratio differences between bounded fractions and secretome controls
experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: In >=3 independent production lots, the bounded capture-positive particle-peak fractions reproducibly show the predefined protected-cargo panel (presence of >=3 miRNA panel members and >=1 luminal protein panel member) and these signals are substantially reduced or abolished after detergent + protease/RNase treatment; concentrated secretome-retaining controls lack this protected pattern or show detergent-insensitive signals. Spike-in tracer recovery confirms assay performance.

explicit_inferences: Inference: Protected-cargo presence on immuno-captured, particle-peak fractions implies membrane protection and association with intact EVs rather than solely soluble co-isolates.
Inference: Reproducibility across lots enables a qualitative lot-gating decision even before numeric specifications are defined.
falsification_criteria: Across >=3 independent production lots, the predefined protected-cargo panel is absent or inconsistent in capture-positive, particle-peak fractions, or panel signals are not reduced by detergent+protease treatment (indicating lack of membrane protection).
Spike-in controls demonstrate assay recovery but endogenous protected-cargo signals remain absent or detergent-insensitive, indicating endogenous signals are not EV-protected.
human_decisions_required: Define the exact miRNA and proteomic panel members (3–6 miRNAs; 2–4 proteins) prior to assay deployment
Approve which fractionation workflow defines the bounded capture-positive particle-peak fraction for the program (SEC+single-cushion vs TFF->SEC->cushion or alternative)
manufacturability_assessment: A focused panel reduces analytical complexity versus whole multi-omic profiling; assay platforms for targeted miRNA panels and targeted proteomics are scalable. Yield requirements and sensitivity for capture-positive fraction omics must be confirmed before treating this as an operational gate.
manufacturing_rationale: A small, conserved protected-cargo panel that is qualitatively reproducible across production lots could be used as a practical, non-numeric comparability gate during early GMP-like scale-up and to prioritize which cargo elements to formalize into potency assays, reducing risk from treating variable secretome signals as EV-specific.
measurement_strategy: Immuno-capture of intact particle fractions (anti-CD63/CD9/CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5) followed by fraction-level particle counting; targeted protected-cargo assays: a small predefined miRNA panel (3–6 candidates) measured by RT-qPCR/targeted sequencing and a small targeted proteomics panel (2–4 luminal proteins) measured by SRM/PRM on captured, detergent±protease-treated material. Use spike-in tracer controls and detergent/protease treatments to assess membrane protection and assay recovery. Qualitative presence/absence calls across lots form the gating decision.
novelty_statement: This hypothesis is novel because it proposes a deliberately small, predefined protected-cargo composite panel (targeted miRNAs + targeted luminal proteins) measured on immuno-captured particle-peak fractions with detergent/protease protection and spike-in recovery controls as a qualitative lot-gating fingerprint. Prior SGL-001 cargo hypotheses focused on broader multi-omic fingerprints or protected-cargo discovery (design-hypothesis-run-20260927T103652Z-0b39f6c9ae58). Here we propose a discriminating, practically scalable, panel-driven testable gate (reduced dimensionality and explicit spike-in controls) intended for early manufacturing comparability decisions rather than open-ended discovery.
principal_risks: Assay sensitivity in low-biomass capture fractions may be insufficient to detect panel elements.
Panel selection may capture non-EV-associated co-isolates, producing false-positive fingerprint reproducibility.
Even if fingerprint reproducible, it may not predict in vivo delivery or functional potency; large-animal delivery uncertainty remains (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution).
proposed_potency_relationship: Exploratory only: conserved protected-cargo fingerprint is a candidate indicator for prioritizing potency linkage experiments; it is NOT asserted as a potency assay nor as evidence of efficacy.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: If supported, define a non-numeric, protected-cargo composite fingerprint (qualitative presence of a predefined panel of membrane-protected miRNAs co-enriched with a small panel of detergent/protease-sensitive luminal proteins in capture-positive particle-peak fractions) as a lot-consistency gating attribute to distinguish an EV-enriched drug-substance from secretome-retaining material.
title: Hypothesis: A protected, particle-associated small-RNA–protein composite fingerprint (focused panel) reproducibly distinguishes EV-associated cargo from variable secretome co-isolates across lots
